chartAdvice.bollean: Bollinger Bands suit range-bound and breakout markets; use EMA 200 to assess the primary trend.
chartAdvice.Donchian: Donchian channels are useful for range-bound and breakout markets.
chartAdvice.ma: MA signals are clearest on daily charts. On weekly charts, MA20 can act as support; confirm higher-timeframe support before trading hourly gaps.
chartAdvice.ema: EMA offers a stable medium- to long-term trend guide on daily charts. For hourly entries, confirm price is near daily EMA60 or SMA200 support.
chartAdvice.atr: ATR Supertrend follows daily trends effectively. For shorter-term use, filter direction with a higher-timeframe EMA to reduce whipsaws in ranges.
chartAdvice.obv: OBV on hourly charts can show fund-flow intent. Compare it with the daily OBV trend before entering a position.
chartAdvice.volume_profile: Volume Profile identifies capital concentration in the visible range. POC is a cost reference; VAH and VAL help identify consolidation or breakouts.
chartAdvice.cci: CCI can identify breakouts and oversold reversals on daily and hourly charts. In short-term use, follow the primary trend.
chartAdvice.mr: MR is designed for intraday momentum and daily exhaustion. Treat a short-term crossover below daily RSI 50 as a rebound trade, not a trend confirmation.
chartAdvice.kd: KD is time-sensitive. Weekly and daily charts offer stronger swing references; short intervals should be filtered with a trend indicator such as MA20.
chartAdvice.mfi: MFI is steadier on daily charts and reacts quickly on hourly charts. An oversold entry should still align with the daily uptrend.
chartAdvice.chip: Positioning data updates after market close and uses institutional, margin, and short data to assess direction.
chartAdvice.ichimoku_cloud: Ichimoku works best on daily and weekly charts. On short intervals, use it with care because indicator noise can dominate.
